Phase 65 plan: docs/phases/hardening-shadow-installs-quiet-upgrades-clean-test-runs.md @ 79de8a1 (branch of the same name, from main @ 3.14.2). The arbiter asked for the remaining hardening items as one phase tonight; four small independent fixes, issues 1, 5, 4 and 10 of docs/tagteam-issues-release-and-venv-upgrade-2026-09-20.md.

1. Shadow installs: doctor + the 'Framework:' line of tagteam state report a tagteam installed in the project's own .venv / venv whose version differs from the running one. lstat-only, no subprocess, no import, a symlinked venv is 'not scanned'; version from the dist-info METADATA; an editable link is listed as 'editable', never as a mismatch (since Phase 64 its label is not the truth); the venv that is sys.prefix is skipped. One warn finding per mismatch, additive 'installs' key in --json, SCHEMA stays 1. Report only.
2. Quiet upgrades: _same_manifest() ignores the top-level 'tagteam' stamp as it already ignores written_at, so a release that changes no framework file stops rewriting the manifest in every project (the 3.14.1 sweep rewrote 41). Per-file 'tagteam' values — what _classify() reads — are untouched.
3. Clean test runs: the wheel_venv fixture builds from a copy of the tree instead of the repo, and asserts it created no build/ or tagteam.egg-info/ there.
4. Diagnosable flake: the watcher-lock waits dump the spawned child's exit code and piped output on timeout. No timeout changed, no claim to fix the flake.

Please press on: (1) is anything reading the manifest's TOP-LEVEL version for a decision (I found display only: framework._version_text and diagnostics.observe_framework) — and is 'last tagteam that changed something here' an acceptable meaning; (2) shadow-install severity warn vs info, and whether skipping sys.prefix and treating editable as non-mismatch are right; (3) reading METADATA inside a venv from doctor — bounded read, lstat chain — any objection; (4) four items in one phase: say so if you would rather I split test hygiene (3, 4) from product code (1, 2).

Verified: tagteam roadmap check ok (66 phases). No code changed; suite not run (plan cycle).

Approved plan at 79de8a1. Keeping these four bounded items together follows the arbiter's requested scope; no split needed.

I checked manifest readers and projected_manifest(): the top-level tagteam stamp is used for display, while classification uses per-file entries, and CURRENT entries preserve their existing provenance. Ignoring only written_at and the top-level tagteam stamp is appropriate. Describe the stamp precisely as the version that last changed the manifest, since seed-only changes need not rewrite it.

The shadow-install warning, additive JSON field, skipping the running sys.prefix, and listing editable installs without asserting a mismatch are appropriate for a report-only diagnostic. Bounded metadata reads through the existing directory-chain guards fit doctor's constraints. Implementation details to preserve: validate each directory before enumerating it (including intermediate lib/python/site-packages and dist-info paths); test nested symlinks as well as a symlinked venv. Treat duplicate/malformed Version headers as unknown, and do not infer that every different version is older: use 'different code/version' wording for a newer installed copy too. Avoid introducing an import cycle between diagnostics and framework when sharing the observation helper.

Building the wheel from an isolated copy addresses the checkout pollution. Make the no-new-artifacts assertion run even on build/install failure or skip. For watcher diagnostics, bound terminate/communicate cleanup and retain a kill fallback so a timeout cannot become a hung gate; distinguish a child already exited from one the helper terminated. The planned immediate-exit regression should verify the emitted output and exit status.

Reviewed plan and relevant source paths; no suite run for this plan cycle.
